root_cause: Two scoring gaps in the charge declaration. (1) _score_charge_target credits the charger's full expected melee damage as ch_damage even beyond the target's remaining wounds, and the probability/short-charge multipliers (x1.2 x1.3 for a 3" charge) then scale that phantom damage. At s7480 r3 P2 the Allarus were credited 7.5 dmg (ch_damage 15) against a 2-wound Allarus remnant 2" away (score 41.96) vs 10 dmg (ch_damage 20) against Blade Champion Alpha with 7 wounds (32.94); with wounds capped the remnant scores 21.6 and the Blade Champion 25.9. (2) _score_multi_target_combo floors an extra target's lock-down share at 0 after subtracting the damage it deals back, so a combo with an extra that adds nothing scores >= the single declaration (it also books the fallback target, which the post-roll re-pick already gives a single declaration in 11e since targets are picked after the roll). The AI therefore declared remnant + Allarus #2 (s7480) and Beast Snagga Boyz (value 0) + Beastboss (s7461). Game-level: in branch B of s7480 the Allarus killed the Blade Champion, which freed Custodian Guard Alpha to fight Blade Champion Gamma, the remnant was left to a weaker unit, the Allarus consolidated to CENTER, and P2 scored Punishment (condemned_left +5) and +5..+9 primary (B-A +11.0 over 2 seeds); in A the big hitter spent its whole fight on 2 wounds.
fix_summary: FIX_CHARGE_TARGET (default 1.0, tag [CHARGE_TARGET]). CH-OVERKILL: in _evaluate_best_charge, when a charger has two or more targets above the 3% skip, _score_charge_target(..., cap_overkill=true) credits melee damage only up to the target's remaining wounds (+ CHARGE_TARGET_OVERKILL_SHARE x excess, default 0; the kill keeps its ch_can_halve/ch_can_wipe bonuses). A charger with one target keeps its old score, so its charge/no-charge call is unchanged. CH-EXTRA: _score_multi_target_combo marks a combo whose non-top member has extra <= 0 (hits back at least its lock-down share) and _evaluate_multi_target_charge skips it; the direct combo scorer is unchanged (its existing test still passes). 0 = base behaviour exactly (both branches gated).

risks: (1) CH-EXTRA is broad in practice: almost every extra target hits back for more than its 0.2 lock-down share, so it removes nearly all multi-target declarations (0 in all 7 fix replays vs 0-2 per game on base). The 11e post-roll re-pick keeps the fallback value, so the main loss is the lock-down of a second unit when both are reached; the gain is fewer multi-target charge moves that fail coherency (seen in s7480 base: a 3-target declaration failed its move) and fewer units hitting the charger in later fight phases. Rounds 3-5: a charger locked with one unit instead of two consolidates/falls back more freely toward objectives (helps primary and Centre Ground / Engage-type secondaries); a second shooter that would have been locked keeps shooting (can cost a unit late). (2) CH-OVERKILL only re-ranks targets for a charger with a choice; it can still lower the best score toward the bar in rare low-value cases (none seen in the 7 replays: every base charge/no-charge call was kept). Late game (round 4-5) finishing a 1-2 wound remnant on an objective is worth OC/primary and kills for destroyed-per-unit secondaries (e.g. Delaying Action destroyed_per_unit): ch_can_wipe (+5), ch_can_halve (+3) and ch_target_on_objective (x1.5, x more in round 4+) are untouched, so a remnant on an objective still competes, but a big hitter will now more often go for the high-wound / character target and leave remnants to cheaper units or shooting; if nothing else can reach the remnant it may survive and score for the enemy. (3) No units are held back (the round-2 failure mode): the fix never turns a charge into no charge by itself and does not touch movement. (4) Not measured over full games; the single bench pair is reach only.
